en: The Apadāna of the Elder Bhaddiya, Son of Kāḷigodhā Upāli Chapter, Number 3 I was once a king named Mahāsudassana, A ruler of the four quarters, a wheel-turning monarch. In that city, Kusāvatī, I dwelt, Possessing the seven treasures and the fourfold army. At that time, there was a Buddha in the world, The Exalted One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One. His name was Kassapa, the peerless, The Teacher of gods and men, the one with vision. He lived in the Deer Park at Rājagaha, Surrounded by a community of monks.

Having heard of the arrival of the Buddha, I went to see the Teacher, the One with Vision. Approaching the Exalted One, I paid homage, And sat down to one side; having sat down, I spoke these words to the Buddha, the One with Vision: "O Blessed One, may you accept my invitation For tomorrow’s meal, together with the community of monks. The Exalted One, the One with Vision, accepted By remaining silent. Then, having understood his consent, I rose from my seat and departed. That very night, having prepared a great feast, I had the city of Kusāvatī adorned. When the morning dawned, I informed the Teacher: "It is time, O Blessed One; the meal is ready. Then, accompanied by the community of monks, The Exalted One, the One with Vision, came. Having arrived, he sat upon the prepared seat, Together with the community of monks. Having offered water for washing the feet, And having served the excellent food, I took a low seat and sat before him. As I sat there, I spoke these words to the Buddha: "I have heard, O Blessed One, that those who offer Food to the Buddhas, the Ones with Vision, Will experience great happiness here in this world, And will attain the bliss of heaven in the next. I wish to know, O Blessed One, the fruit Of this gift of almsfood. What is the result of giving food? May the One with Vision explain it to me. The Exalted One, the One with Vision, replied: "Listen well, O King, and pay close attention. I shall explain to you the fruit of giving food, Both in this world and in the life to come. One who gives food with a joyful heart, Freed from hunger and thirst, becomes wise. Endowed with strength and beauty, They become a lord of the earth, a wheel-turning monarch. Having passed away from that human state, They are reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three. There they enjoy divine pleasures, Adorned with celestial garments and garlands. From that realm, when their merit is exhausted, They pass away and are reborn among humans. There too they are born into a noble family, With great wealth and abundant grain. Thus, O King, is the fruit of giving food, Both in this world and in the life to come. Therefore, one should always give with joy, Seeking the welfare of both this world and the next. Having heard the Buddha’s teaching, My mind became serene and clear. I made a vow before the One with Vision: "May I too become a Buddha like you, A teacher of gods and men, the One with Vision. Through that root of merit, the deed I performed, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three. There I enjoyed divine pleasures, Adorned with celestial garments and garlands. Passing away from that realm, I was reborn as a human, In a wealthy family of the Sakyans. Now I am known as Bhaddiya, The son of Kāḷigodhā. Having seen the suffering of birth and death, I have gone forth into homelessness. Today, I have attained the goal, The state of an Arhat, free from all taints. This is the fruit of giving food, Both in this world and in the life to come. Therefore, one should always give with joy, Seeking the welfare of both this world and the next. Thus did the Elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā, Speak of his own past deeds. Having heard this, the monks were filled with wonder, And they praised the Elder’s noble conduct. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā.
“The entire multitude of people approaches the Sambuddha Padumuttara,
the Great Sage whose mind is filled with loving-kindness.”
To the supreme leader of the entire world. And Sattuka and Baddhaka,
with food, drink, and provisions;
All give to the Teacher,
the unsurpassed field of merit;
I too shall give a gift.
Having invited the Best of Buddhas, the God of Gods,
the Tathāgata, as well as the unsurpassed Saṅgha.
Having been dismissed by me,
they invited the Tathāgata and the entire community of monks.
The unsurpassed field of merit.
A couch of a hundred thousand [pieces of gold],
made of gold and spread with a woolen coverlet;
With a coverlet of fine wool and cotton,
I prepared a most costly bed.
The seat was prepared for the Buddha.
Padumuttara, the knower of the world,
the god of gods, the bull among men;
Surrounded by the community of bhikkhus, he approached my door;
having gone out to meet the Sambuddha, I...
To the world-protector of great renown,
with a clear mind and joyful heart,
I offered a canopy.
With a serene heart and a joyful mind, [I saw] a hundred thousand bhikkhus and the Buddha, the Leader of the World.
I satisfied him with the finest food.
Padumuttara, the Knower of the World,
the recipient of offerings;
Having sat down in the community of bhikkhus,
he spoke these verses:
“By whom this seat was given, [to him I speak].”
It was made of gold and spread with a woolen coverlet;
I shall describe it to you,
so listen as I speak.
Seventy-four times he will exercise sovereignty over the gods;
he shall experience such prosperity.
Honored by celestial nymphs,
he shall dwell upon the earth, possessing a thousand local kingdoms.
And fifty-one times he will become a wheel-turning monarch.
In all states of existence and wombs,
He will be born into a high-born family;
and having later gone forth into homelessness,
he will be impelled by the root of his wholesome merit.
"One named Bhaddiya shall become a disciple of the Teacher;
I am devoted to solitude."
I have dwelt in the forest hermitage;
having attained all the fruits,
today I am one who has abandoned the defilements.
Having directly known everything,
the Omniscient One, the Leader of the World,
sat down amidst the community of monks.
He placed me in this foremost position:
"The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]."
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, indeed, the Elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā, spoke these verses.
This is the third legend of the Elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā.
